caption:
Most people start automating the wrong thing. They pick the task that annoys them most, not the one that pays back fastest.

Four filters that work better.

1. Anything you do every day. Frequency beats complexity. A two-minute task done daily costs more per year than a two-hour task done twice.

2. Anything you copy and paste. Copy-paste is a signal that the same data already exists somewhere else and is being moved by hand.

3. Anything with a deadline you can miss. Not because a machine is smarter, but because it doesn't forget.

4. The follow-up nobody enjoys sending. It gets skipped when you're busy — which is exactly when it matters.

Everything else can wait. Start with these four and the rest of the list gets shorter on its own.

Which one is costing you the most right now?
